Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 94–95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾, meaning: proclaim what you are commanded, that is, convey the message of God to all creation so that the proof may be established against them, for God has commanded you to do so. Al-sad' (ṣadʿ) means splitting. "Tasaddaʿa al-qawm" means the people scattered, and from it [comes] "On that Day they will be divided" [see vol. 14, p. 21], meaning they will scatter. "Sadaʿtuhu fa-nsadaʿa" means I split it and it split apart. The origin of ṣadʿ is separation and splitting. Abu Dhu'ayb said, describing the wild donkey and his she-asses:

"And as if they were a gaming-arrow case, and he was like a gambler (yasar) pouring out over the arrows and splitting them."

[Al-rababa: the hide in which the arrows are gathered. Al-yasar: the owner of the maysir game who strikes with the arrows.]

That is, he separates and splits. As for His saying, "So proclaim openly what you are commanded," al-Farra' said: He meant "fa-sdaʿ bi-l-amr," that is, make your religion manifest. On this reading, "ma" with the verb is in the position of a verbal noun. Ibn al-A'rabi said: the meaning of "isdaʿ bi-ma tu'mar" is "iqsid," that is, aim/proceed directly. It was also said: "fa-sdaʿ bi-ma tu'mar" means divide their assembly and their word by calling them to monotheism, for they will split apart, with some answering and others not. On this view, the splitting refers back to the splitting of the group of disbelievers.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, meaning: do not concern yourself with their mockery and do not heed their words, for God has cleared you of what they say. Ibn ʿAbbas said: this is abrogated by His saying, "Then kill the polytheists" [see vol. 8, p. 72]. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUbayd said: the Prophet ﷺ remained hidden until the verse ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾ was revealed, and so he and his companions went out. Mujahid said: it means raising the voice with the Qur'an in prayer. "And turn away from the polytheists" means do not be concerned with them. Ibn Ishaq said: When they persisted in evil and greatly mocked the Messenger of God ﷺ, God the Exalted revealed: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers, those who set up another god with God; but they will come to know﴾. The meaning is: proclaim what you are commanded and do not fear anyone other than God, for God is sufficient to protect you from their harm, as He sufficed you against the mockers. They were five of the leaders of the people of Makkah: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who was their chief, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, Abu Zam'a, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, and al-Harith ibn al-Talatila. God destroyed them all, it is said on the day of Badr, on a single day, because of their mockery of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The cause of their destruction, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, was that Gabriel came to the Messenger of God ﷺ while they were circling the House; he stood, and the Messenger of God ﷺ stood with him. Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him and threw a green leaf in his face, and he went blind and his eye was in pain, so he began striking his head against the wall. Al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth passed by him and pointed at his belly, and his belly swelled with water and he died of it, bloated (ḥabanan). (It is said: habina (with kasra) habanan, and the passive huibina, meaning his belly became enlarged with yellow water, so he is ahban, and the woman is habna'; so said in al-Sihah.) Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira passed by him and pointed at the trace of a wound at the bottom of his ankle, which he had received years before, while he was dragging his trailing garment (sabal) [al-sabal (with vowel): garments worn trailing, done out of arrogance and conceit]. This was because he passed by a man from Khuza'a who was fletching his arrows, and an arrow from his quiver caught on his garment and scratched his leg with that scratch, which was nothing, but it festered and killed him. Al-As ibn Wa'il passed by him and pointed at the sole of his foot, so he went out on his donkey heading for al-Ta'if; he rode it over a sabrag bush [al-sabraq: a edible Hijazi plant with thorns], and a thorn entered the sole of his foot and killed him. Al-Harith ibn al-Talatila passed by him and pointed at his head, so he discharged pus [al-makhkh: flowing out] and was killed. There is a difference of reports regarding the cause of their deaths close to this. It was also said that they are the intended meaning of God's saying: ﴿the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾ [see p. 97 of this volume], likening what befell them in their deaths to the roof falling upon them, as will come.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted﴾, meaning your heart, because the breast is the place of the heart.

(﴿at what they say﴾), meaning: at what you hear of their denial of you and their rejection of your words, and what reaches you. And what your companions suffer from your enemies.

**First issue (1):** Concerning this, there are two points.

**The first point:** His saying, the Exalted, (So glorify [Allah]) means: so take refuge in prayer, for it is the ultimate form of glorification and the highest sanctification. This explains His saying: (and be among those who prostrate). There is no doubt that the greatest nearness [to Allah] in prayer is during prostration, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The closest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so increase [the supplication]" [[The narration is "fa-akthiru" (so increase), as in al-Jami' al-Saghir.]]. For this reason, He specifically mentioned prostration.

**The second point:** Ibn al-'Arabi said: Some people thought that the command here refers to prostration itself, so they considered this place to be a place of prostration in the Qur'an. I saw the imam at the mihrab (prayer niche) of Zechariah in the Holy House, may Allah purify it, prostrating at this place, and I prostrated with him there, but the majority of scholars do not consider it [a place of prostration]. I say: Abu Bakr al-Naqqash mentioned that there is a prostration here according to Abu Hudhayfa and Yaman ibn Ri'ab, and he held that it is obligatory.

His saying, the Exalted: (And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty) (99). Concerning this there is one issue: the certainty is death. He commanded him to worship [Allah], since his servants fall short in His service, and this is obligatory upon him. If it is asked: What is the benefit of saying "until there comes to you the certainty," when "And worship your Lord" would have sufficed for the command to worship? It is said: The benefit is that if He had said "And worship your Lord" without qualification, and he worshipped once, he would have been obedient; but when He says "until there comes to you the certainty," its meaning is: do not leave this until you die. If it is asked: Why did He, glorified is He, say "And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty" and not say "forever"? The answer is that "the certainty" is more emphatic than saying "forever," because the word "forever" may refer to a single moment or to the whole of eternity. This meaning has already been discussed [[See vol. 2, p. 33.]]. The intended meaning is the continuation of worship throughout his life, as the righteous servant said: "And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive" [cf. Qur'an 19:31].

From this it follows that if a man says to his wife, "You are divorced forever," and then says, "I intended a day or a month," then he may take her back (rij'ah, i.e., returning to a divorced wife). But if he says, "I divorced her for her lifetime," he may not take her back.

The evidence that the certainty is death is the hadith of Umm al-'Ala al-Ansariyya, who was among those who pledged allegiance, and in it: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "As for Uthman, I mean Uthman ibn Maz'un, the certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him. By Allah, though I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not know what will be done with him." And he mentioned the hadith [[See Sahih al-Bukhari, vol. 3, p. 151, Bulaq edition.]]. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, may Allah have mercy on him!

Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz used to say: "I have not seen a certainty more like doubt than the people's certainty about death, and then they do not prepare for it," meaning, as if they were doubtful about it.

It has also been said that the certainty here is the truth that has no doubt in it, [referring to] your victory over your enemies. Ibn Shajara said: "The first view is more correct, and it is the view of Mujahid, Qatada and al-Hasan." And Allah knows best.

Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated from Abu Muslim al-Khawlani that he heard him say: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "It was not revealed to me to gather wealth and be among the merchants; rather, it was revealed to me: Glorify with the praise of your Lord, and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty."
